Ryedale's population increased by around 3,000 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 55,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Ryedale increased by 5.7%, from just under 51,800 in 2011 to around 54,700 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of Yorkshire and The Humber (3.7%), but by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Ryedale was home to around 0.3 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 0.2 in 2011. This area was the joint second-least densely populated local authority area across England (after Eden).

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in Ryedale than across Yorkshire and The Humber

An older Ryedale

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Ryedale increased by three years, from 47 to 50 years of age.

This area had the joint highest average (median) age in Yorkshire and The Humber (alongside Craven, Hambleton and Scarborough) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 65 to 74 years rose by just over 1,600 (an increase of 25.2%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by around 1,600 (15.8% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 65 and 74 years increased by 2.3 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

More divorces and dissolved civil partnerships

Ryedale saw England's second-largest percentage-point rise in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership (from 8.7% in 2011 to 9.8% in 2021).

England's largest increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership occurred in Richmondshire (from 8.2% to 9.4%).

Across Yorkshire and The Humber, the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 9.3% to 9.4%, while the percentage in nearby Scarborough increased from 10.8% to 11.6%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership in Ryedale increased by 1.1 percentage points

Unpaid care in Ryedale

Ryedale saw Yorkshire and The Humber's joint second-largest percentage-point fall (alongside Hambleton and Harrogate) in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care (from 7.9% in 2011 to 4.9% in 2021). These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

Across the region, only Craven saw a greater fall in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care (from 8.4% to 5.0%).

Every local authority area across Yorkshire and The Humber saw a fall in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care, as the regional proportion fell from 7.1% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Ryedale decreased by 3.0 percentage points

Disability in Ryedale

Ryedale saw Yorkshire and The Humber's second-largest percentage-point rise in the proportion of residents who were identified as disabled and limited a little (from 9.1% in 2011 to 10.0% in 2021). These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

Across the region, only York saw a greater rise in the proportion of residents who were identified as disabled and limited a little (from 9.5% to 10.9%).

Across Yorkshire and The Humber, the proportion of residents who were identified as disabled and limited a little increased from 10.5% to 10.7%, while the proportion in nearby Scarborough increased from 10.8% to 11.6%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a little in Ryedale increased by 0.9 percentage points

Religion in Ryedale

In 2021, 34.2% of Ryedale residents reported having "No religion", up from 20.0% in 2011. The rise of 14.2 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Ryedale. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across Yorkshire and The Humber, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 25.9% to 39.4%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 58.7% of people in Ryedale described themselves as Christian (down from 71.8%), while 6.0% did not state their religion (down from 7.4% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 34.2% of usual residents in Ryedale reported having "No religion"

Ryedale residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 50,500 Ryedale residents said they were born in England. This represented 92.2% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 48,300 in 2011, which at the time represented 93.3% of Ryedale's population.

Scotland was the next most represented, with around 900 Ryedale residents reporting this country of birth (1.7%). This figure has remained relatively unchanged from 2011.

The number of Ryedale residents born in Poland rose from just over 200 in 2011 (0.4% of the local population) to around 400 in 2021 (0.7%).

In 2021, 92.2% of Ryedale residents reported their country of birth as England

Change in employment

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater in Ryedale (3.1 percentage points) than across England (0.8 percentage points).

In Ryedale, the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) decreased from 58.1% in 2011 to 55.0% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage across England decreased from 56.5% to 55.7%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were unemployed (excluding full-time students) in Ryedale fell from 2.4% to 1.6%, while the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were retired (economically inactive) increased from 28.1% to 30.6%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Ryedale decreased by 3.1 percentage points

Change in work hours

In 2021, 11.9% of Ryedale residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 11.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in seven people (15.4%) said they worked over 49 hours per week, compared with 17.7% in 2011. The percentage of adults in employment working 31 to 48 hours per week increased from 50.3% to 51.9%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week was 9.7% (similar to 2011) across Yorkshire and The Humber. Across England, the percentage increased from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Ryedale increased by 0.3 percentage points

Health in Ryedale

In 2021, 50.0% of Ryedale residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 48.3% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 34.9% to 34.3%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Ryedale residents describing their health as "very bad" remained 0.9%, while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 3.2% to 3.0%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

In 2021, 0.9% of usual residents said their health was very bad in Ryedale

Ethnic groups in Ryedale

In 2021, 0.8% of Ryedale residents identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category, up from 0.6% in 2011. The 0.2 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across Yorkshire and The Humber, the percentage of people from "Mixed or Multiple ethnic groups" increased from 1.6% to 2.1%, while across England the percentage increased from 2.3% to 3.0%.

In 2021, 98.2% of people in Ryedale identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 98.7% in 2011), while 0.6% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (compared with 0.5% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 0.1% in 2011 to 0.3% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 0.8% of usual residents in Ryedale identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category

Change in housing in Ryedale

Of Ryedale households, 66.8% owned their home in 2021, down from 67.1% in 2011.

The decrease in the percentage of households that owned their home was greater across Yorkshire and The Humber (1.5 percentage points, from 64.1% to 62.6%) than in Ryedale (0.4 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 2.0 percentage points, from 63.3% to 61.3%.

The rate of home ownership in Ryedale decreased by 0.4 percentage points

National identity in Ryedale

In 2021, 3.2% of Ryedale residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 2.4% in 2011.

In 2021, 0.9% of residents identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.4% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Ryedale that identified as "British only" increased from 14.6% to 57.9%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across Yorkshire and The Humber (1.6 percentage points, from 5.1% to 6.7%) than in Ryedale (0.9 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Ryedale increased by 0.9 percentage points

Family in Ryedale

Of Ryedale households, 21.4% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 22.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in six households (16.2%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 18.0% in 2011. The percentage of single family households including a couple living with only non-dependent children decreased from 6.4% to 6.2%.

This area had the region’s third highest percentage of households including a couple but no children. Across the region, only Selby (22.3%) and Richmondshire (21.5%) had a higher percentage of households including a couple but no children.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Ryedale decreased by 1.2 percentage points
